sentences.text: As per compromise, applicant and respondent No.2 have decided to withdraw all the proceedings pending against each.
Now applicant has filed this Petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashment of FIR.
3. Counsel for the respondent No.2 submits that he has withdrawn almost cases filed against the applicant.
Certainly, he has no objection to quash the FIR.

4. In view of above, FIR dated 02.02.2023 registered at Crime No.95/2023 at Police Station Rajendranagar, District Indore for the offence punishable under Section 467, 323, 504, 506, 292m 420, 500 of IPC is hereby quashed.

5. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant submits that some news contents of dispute of applicant and respondent No.2 are surfaced in the social media, thus direction may be given to Cyber Crime Department to delete the same.

6. The Cyber Crime Department of State of Madhya Pradesh is directed to take steps for deletion of contents of dispute of applicant and respondent No.2 for which permission is required from applicant and respondent No.2, same shall be given.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The complainant/applicant herself filed this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashment of FIR dated 02.02.2023 registered at Crime No.95/2023 at Police Station Rajendranagar, District Indore for the offence punishable under Section 467, 323, 504, 506, 292m 420, 500 of IPC.
The applicant and respondent No.2 both have filed number of Criminal Cases, Civil Cases and Matrimonial Cases against each other, wisdom prevail and they have entered into compromise as observed by the High Court of Judicature at Bombay in Anticipatory Bail Application NO.3319/2022 (Annexure P-2).
As per compromise, applicant and respondent No.2 have decided to withdraw all the proceedings pending against each.
Now applicant has filed this Petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashment of FIR.
